references.text: Jesus quotes and interprets the text from Deuteronomy that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word from God. Here, the bread from heaven is directly linked to life-giving power distinct from the physical nourishment the fathers received.
The text in Psalms describes how God gave manna from heaven and let people eat angel's food. This is the most detailed Old Testament description of the manna that Jesus refers to in his comparison.
Here Israel remembers that God gave them bread from heaven. The text emphasizes God's providence that gives life, a theme Jesus develops by saying that whoever eats this bread will live forever.

The Letter to the Hebrews refers to the same generation that ate manna and died, using this as a warning against losing faith. This mirrors Jesus' contrast between the death of the fathers and eternal life in him.
